en: Rough volcanic rocks in Taal create high friction, making it difficult for hikers to slip on the trails.
Gravity pulls the water of Maria Cristina Falls downward, converting potential energy into kinetic energy.
The lower jaw of a crocodile acts as a third-class lever when it snaps shut to catch fish.
Black sand beaches in Cagayan contain magnetite, a naturally magnetic mineral that a compass can detect.
Frequent lightning strikes in the Philippines occur when static electricity discharges between storm clouds and the ground.
Fireflies in mangrove forests produce cold light through a chemical reaction called bioluminescence to attract mates.
Sound travels faster through the ocean water of the Tubbataha Reef than through the air above it.
Geothermal heat from Mount Makiling warms the underground water that flows out as hot springs in Calamba.
A falling coconut from a tall palm tree converts gravitational potential energy into kinetic energy.
The sloping trunk of a coconut palm acts as an inclined plane for tree-climbing crabs to reach the top.
A river otter's sleek fur traps air to reduce water friction while it swims through local streams.
The gravitational pull of the moon causes the ocean water in Manila Bay to rise and fall.
